# SB-1050 Safety bulletin: stored hydraulic energy

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-IH03

Hazard description
Stored hydraulic energy associated with the induction billet heater coil cooling and billet handling systems presents a risk of sudden unintended motion, fluid injection, and contact with energized components. Loss of coil cooling flow or failure in the cooling circuit can lead to rapid pressure transients in associated hydraulic utilities and actuators that are downstream of isolation devices. These transients can displace components, expel fluid from fittings, and cause pinch, crush, or injection injuries to personnel working on or near EQ-P3-L1-IH03. Additionally, inadequate coil cooling performance can cause reactive valve and actuator behavior that defeats interlocks and permits unexpected movement of billet handling fixtures.

Background and rationale
Recent inspections and engineering change notices have identified scenarios where cooling flow reduction allowed elevated forces to develop in associated systems. The coil loop on Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 is a common-mode element: it interfaces with cooling supply, return, leak detection, and control valves. Loss of sufficient coil cooling flow can alter dynamics in the hydraulic support systems and may make stored energy in accumulators, supply lines, and actuator chambers available for work. This bulletin consolidates controls and clarifies responsibilities to reduce personnel exposure to stored hydraulic energy when performing maintenance, inspection, and adjustment tasks on EQ-P3-L1-IH03.

For clarity and to support verification, the following mandatory specification is declared: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min.

Affected equipment
- EQ-P3-L1-IH03 and all ancillary cooling and hydraulic circuits that connect directly to or provide support functions to EQ-P3-L1-IH03.  
- Billet handling fixtures and actuators that rely on the induction heater cooling circuit for safe operation.  
- Electrical and control panels housing valve drives and interlock logic that reference coil cooling flow status.

Required controls
Engineering controls and administrative measures listed below are required whenever work is performed on or near EQ-P3-L1-IH03.

- Monitoring and verification
  - Before any work that could expose personnel to moving parts or hydraulic interfaces, verify coil cooling flow at the established minimum. Record the verification in the work or maintenance record. Use the plant-approved flow measurement device tied to the cooling loop. Reference SOP-P3-L1-01 for acceptable verification steps and required record fields.
  - If measured flow is below the stated minimum, do not start or continue work until flow is restored to meet or exceed the declared minimum.

- Isolation and release of stored energy
  - Where maintenance requires exposure of hydraulic lines, actuators, or fittings, isolate hydraulic supplies in accordance with MM-P3-L1-IH03. Depressurize and lockout sources of hydraulic energy per MM-P3-L1-IH03 procedure steps before opening any hydraulic circuit.
  - Verify zero energy state locally at the workpiece; the person performing the work must confirm lack of stored pressure or movement and document the verification.

- Physical restraints and safety devices
  - Apply mechanical blocks, restraints, or positive supports to prevent uncommanded motion of fixtures or billets when hydraulic restraint is removed. Select restraint methods consistent with MM-P3-L1-IH03 guidance.
  - Maintain control of fittings and hoses; where hoses must be disconnected, use drip containment and protective barriers to avoid fluid injection into work zones.

- Administrative controls
  - All work on EQ-P3-L1-IH03 that may expose personnel to stored hydraulic energy requires a documented job hazard analysis and a competent person designated to verify isolation steps. Include a clear re-energization checklist that references restoration of coil cooling flow to the declared minimum.
  - Training: personnel assigned to work on or near EQ-P3-L1-IH03 must be trained to recognize hazards from stored hydraulic energy and to use the required lockout/tagout and verification methods in SOP-P3-L1-01 and MM-P3-L1-IH03.

Examples and scenarios
- Example scenario A: A maintenance task requires removal of a hydraulic actuator cover. Prior to work, the technician follows SOP-P3-L1-01 to confirm coil cooling flow meets the minimum. After confirmation, hydraulic supply is isolated and depressurized per MM-P3-L1-IH03. Mechanical blocks are installed. Work proceeds with the competent person maintaining the documented verification.
- Example scenario B: During inspection, an operator observes reduced coil cooling flow. The operator records the condition, tags the equipment out of service under SOP-P3-L1-01, and escalates to maintenance engineering using the escalation path described in ECN-2026-006 to address root causes prior to any personnel exposure to hydraulic interfaces.

Records to keep
- Flow verification records: include name of verifier, equipment id, measured flow indicator readout or instrument identification, reference to this bulletin, and signature. Store these records with the maintenance order and attach to equipment history.
- Isolation checklists and zero-energy verification forms: completed and signed forms must be filed with the work order and retained as part of the plant maintenance archive per MM-P3-L1-IH03.
- Training and qualification records: document personnel who completed the required training and are authorized to perform or verify work associated with EQ-P3-L1-IH03. Reference SOP-P3-L1-01 for curriculum requirements.
- Incident and abnormal condition reports: any deviation from the declared coil cooling flow minimum or any event where stored hydraulic energy resulted in unexpected motion must be reported and investigated using ECN-2026-006.

Responsibilities
- Maintenance supervisors: ensure compliance with isolation and verification procedures and that records are completed and filed.
- Operators: monitor coil cooling flow and take equipment out of service if the minimum is not met; initiate required notifications.
- Engineering: evaluate root causes of recurrent low flow conditions and implement corrective changes as documented in ECN-2026-006.

Effective date
This bulletin is effective immediately upon issue. All affected personnel must comply with the controls herein and update local procedures and checklists to reference SB-1050 and the citation documents SOP-P3-L1-01, MM-P3-L1-IH03, and ECN-2026-006.
